raw_evidence.locator: d2lib/d2.go, compileInput function, line 77 (called only by Compile, never by Parse)

raw_evidence.quote: Never use the presence of the output file to check for success.  Always use the exit status of d2.  This is because sometimes when errors occur while rendering, d2 still write out a partial render anyway to enable iteration on a broken diagram.

validator_existence_and_exit_code.rationale: A dedicated `d2 validate file.d2` subcommand exists (confirmed both in source and in the man page). Any error returned by `validateCmd` — including a parse error — propagates to `mainFatal`, which calls `os.Exit(code)` with `code` defaulting to 1 unless the error is a typed `ExitError` carrying a different explicit code. This is a genuine deterministic non-zero exit on a malformed file, suitable in principle for a CI gate, matching the survey's validator requirement.

semantic_vs_syntax_checking.citation: d2lib/d2.go lines 54-67 (Parse calls only d2parser.Parse; Compile is the separate function that calls d2compiler.Compile)
semantic_vs_syntax_checking.rationale: The `validate` subcommand calls `d2lib.Parse`, which is a thin wrapper around `d2parser.Parse` only — pure syntax/AST parsing. It never calls `d2compiler.Compile`, the function that performs semantic resolution (shape/connection graph construction, layout preparation, and whatever internal consistency checks the compiler performs). Full semantic compilation only happens on the render path (`d2 file.d2 out.svg`), not on `d2 validate`. So `d2 validate` catches syntax errors but not the class of semantic issue the research question named as the test case (a connection to an undeclared shape) — and that specific test case is moot in D2 regardless, since D2's connection syntax auto-declares any shape it references (a documented core language feature, not an error condition), so there is no 'undeclared shape' error class for D2 to check in the first place. Classified as expressible-only-via-workaround because getting any semantic-level error surfaced as a CI-gate-worthy exit code requires running the full render command instead of the dedicated validate command, and even then the specific semantic check the question was probing for (undeclared-shape references) does not exist as an error class in this language by design.

contrary_evidence_search.result: No official documentation page describes validate's exit-code contract more precisely than the man page's general 'always use the exit status' guidance and the source code itself; the distinction between validate's Parse-only path and the render command's Compile path is not called out anywhere in the prose documentation — it was found only by reading the source directly. This is recorded as a documentation gap: a user relying on prose docs alone would not learn that `validate` performs syntax-only checking.
